title: Interleaved prefetch conductor and eviction safeguard for paged KV
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an Interleaved Prefetch Conductor (IPC) that coordinates anticipatory prefill across paged KV shards and adds a lightweight eviction-safeguard token so decode-time kernel selection is less likely to encounter hot-miss storms. Goal: reduce p99 prefill latency spikes and end-to-end decode tail without increasing average token cost materially.
acceptance_criteria: IPC runs in serving path with <3% added CPU overhead per shard under 95th percentile QPS
p99 prefill latency for 1k-2k token prefill workloads reduced by >=25% in synthetic replay
overall token compute cost variance does not increase >5% compared to baseline
no regression in correctness or KV consistency; unit + integration tests added
can be toggled per-tenant and observed in Console dashboards with new metrics
perf_baseline: Baseline: p99 prefill latency = 248ms (1k token prefill, mixed-tenant trace). Cold-KV miss rate = 18%. Average per-token compute cost = 1.00x baseline unit. Target: p99 <= 186ms, miss rate <= 12%
investigation_notes: 2026-02-12: Spike replay experiments show that naive aggressive prefill lowers miss rate but increases average tail compute by ~9% due to unnecessary warmups
2026-02-18: Implemented per-shard soft-reservations (token credits) to bound prefill overhead; initial runs reduce p99 by 18% while adding 2.1% CPU
2026-02-25: Added staleness scoring (time since last use + reuse-score) to avoid prefetching cold fragments for long-tail tenants — reduced unnecessary prefetch by 40%

2026-03-03: Kernel-level handshake added: IPC emits an eviction-safeguard token that deprioritizes immediate evictions for prefetched fragments for 50-200ms window. This prevents decode-time thrash when back-to-back requests hit nearby shards
2026-03-07: Nightly canary on internal dedicated pool (10 nodes) shows p99 prefill latency 184ms, cold miss rate 10.4%, CPU delta 2.6% — meets targets in canary
decisions: Use a probabilistic soft-reservation (credit-based) rather than strict pinning to avoid long-term memory bloat
Eviction safeguard token implemented as a short-lived priority bump attached to fragment metadata (50-200ms TTL configurable)
IPC runs as a cooperative user-space scheduler inside the runtime worker thread so no extra process-level orchestration is required
Telemetry: add fragment-prefetch-reason tag (predictive|reactive|manual) to existing KV metrics for downstream analysis
risks: Over-prefetch could increase GPU memory pressure under extreme multi-tenant scenarios if soft-reservations accumulate; mitigated by global admission cap
Eviction-safeguard TTL too long could cause eviction starvation for higher-priority tenants — will be capped and observable via new metric
Interference with existing kernel co-placement heuristics; added compatibility tests but kernel scheduler might need follow-up tuning
next_steps: Finish PR 5310 to add eviction-safeguard token plumbing and unit tests
Add Console dashboard panels: fragment_prefetch_rate, eviction_safeguard_hits, prefetch_cpu_delta
Run larger scale canary across dedicated cluster (50 nodes) and collect staleness/tail histograms
Schedule cross-team review with Kernel team to validate no regression in kernel selection for short sequences
